S63.01.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
S63.01.note: The gallery only shows when the account can create schedules; Free accounts see a lock message instead.
steps: Tap the Open menu button (it has no visible text) and tap Schedules.
Scroll to the bottom of the list. If there are no routines, the empty screen shows the gallery.
Look under the heading Try a template for the ready-made cards (for example Weekly review).
Tap a card and check that the Create form opens with that template filled in.
S63.01.where: Open menu > Schedules > scroll to the bottom > Try a template

S63.02.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
S63.02.note: The arrow button is an icon with no visible text; its accessibility label is Continue scheduling task.
steps: Open Schedules from the Open menu.
Tap the Schedule a task box at the bottom and type a prompt, for example: Summarise today's news headlines.
Tap the arrow button (Continue scheduling task), type a time such as Every day at 9am in When should it run?, then tap Create Schedule.
Check that a new card with your prompt appears in the list.
S63.02.where: Open menu > Schedules > Schedule a task box at the bottom > Continue scheduling task (arrow) > Create Schedule

S63.05.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
steps: Open Schedules and tap the + icon at the top right (accessibility label Create schedule).
Tap the Prompt box and type several lines of instructions; press return to start a new line.
Tap Create Schedule, then tap the new card to open it for editing.
Check that the Prompt box still shows the full multi-line text, then change one line and tap Save Changes.

S63.11.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
steps: Open Schedules, tap the + icon (Create schedule).
Under Recurrence tap Once, then tap the Date field and pick a future date.
Set Preferred time, enter a name and prompt, then tap Create Schedule.
Check that the card shows Once on <month> <day> at <time> and that Next run shows a future time.
S63.11.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > Recurrence > Once > Date

S63.12.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
S63.12.note: The card note says runs are checked on a sweep, so a run can start later in the Cloud window.
steps: Open Schedules, tap the + icon (Create schedule).
Under Recurrence tap Daily, Weekly or Monthly. For Weekly tap the day chips (Su to Sa); for Monthly pick a Day of Month.
Set Preferred time, enter a name and prompt, then tap Create Schedule.
Check the card text: Daily at <time>, Every <days> at <time>, or Monthly on the <n>th at <time>, and that Next run changes to match.
S63.12.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > Recurrence > Daily, Weekly or Monthly

S63.13.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
steps: Open Schedules, tap the + icon (Create schedule) and scroll down to the Time zone field.
Tap the Time zone field (accessibility label starts with Time zone:), type a city in Search time zones, and pick a zone.
Set a Preferred time, then tap Create Schedule.
Tap the card to edit it and check that Time zone still shows the zone you picked.
S63.13.where: Open menu > Schedules > + (Create schedule) > scroll down to Time zone

S63.19.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine that is switched on
S63.19.note: A paused routine has no Run now; the card hint says Resume this schedule to run it now.
steps: Open Schedules and find a routine whose switch is on.
Tap its More actions button (...), then tap Run now.
Watch the card: it shows Starting... and the History section opens.
Check that a new run row appears in Run History with a status and time, and that Last run updates once it finishes.
S63.19.where: Open menu > Schedules > card's More actions (...) button > Run now

S63.20.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
steps: Open Schedules and look at the bottom left of a card.
Read the Next run text (for example in 2h, tomorrow, Overdue or Not scheduled).
Pause the routine with its switch, then check that the text changes to show it will not run.
Resume it and check that the text shows a time again.
S63.20.where: Open menu > Schedules > card, line Next run

S63.21.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine that has run at least once
steps: Open Schedules and read the line under each card's prompt.
Check the text: Last run <time ago>, Last run failed <time ago> (in red), or Not run yet.
Run a routine with Run now and check the line updates after the run.
Compare with Expected: the line should show when it last ran and whether it failed.
S63.21.where: Open menu > Schedules > card, line under the prompt

S63.22.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine that has runs
S63.22.note: The card shows the latest five runs; the full list is on the Scheduled runs screen.
steps: Open Schedules and tap History at the bottom right of a card.
Read the Run History list under the card: each row shows a status, a duration and a time.
Tap the refresh icon (Refresh run history) to reload.
Tap the clock icon at the top (Scheduled runs) to see runs from all routines, and compare with Expected.
S63.22.where: Open menu > Schedules > card > History > Run History

S63.23.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine with a finished run that has output
S63.23.note: There is no separate run page; the output shows inside the run row, and the Scheduled runs rows open the routine editor instead.
steps: Open Schedules, tap History on a card that has runs.
Look at a run row: the result text appears under its status line, up to six lines.
Long-press the result text to select it, or tap the flag icon (Report this run) if you want to report it.
Compare with Expected: the row should show what that run produced, not only its status.
S63.23.where: Open menu > Schedules > card > History > run row text

S63.24.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
steps: Open Schedules and turn off the switch at the top right of a card.
Check that the card stays in the list and its Next run text changes.
Tap its More actions button (...) and tap Resume.
Check the switch is on again and the routine was not deleted.
S63.24.where: Open menu > Schedules > card switch (top right) or More actions (...) > Pause / Resume

S63.26.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
S63.26.note: A routine with an unsupported cadence shows Edit this cadence on Web and cannot be edited on mobile.
steps: Open Schedules and tap a card's body, or open its More actions button (...) and tap Edit.
Change the Schedule Name, the Preferred time or the prompt.
Tap Save Changes.
Reopen the same card and check the new values are shown on the card and in the form.
S63.26.where: Open menu > Schedules > tap the card (or More actions (...) > Edit) > Save Changes

S63.27.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on
S63.27.note: The edit form also has a Delete Schedule button that goes to the same dialog.
steps: Open Schedules and tap a card's More actions button (...), then tap Delete.
Read the Delete schedule? dialog, then tap Cancel and check the card is still there.
Repeat, and tap Delete in the dialog.
Check the card disappears from the list and its Run History no longer appears.
S63.27.where: Open menu > Schedules > card's More actions (...) > Delete > Delete schedule?

S63.32.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a scheduled run that is waiting for approval
S63.32.note: The approval request is created by the server during an unattended run, so a tester cannot start one from the app; the approval block itself is in apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleRunHistory.tsx.
steps: Open Schedules and find a card that says Paused for your approval, so approve or deny it in History.
Tap History on that card.
Find the run row marked Needs approval and read the tool action it asks for.
Tap Approve, then check the run continues; or tap Deny and check the run stops.
S63.32.where: Open menu > Schedules > card text Paused for your approval > History > Needs approval > Approve or Deny

S63.33.needs: a paid account (Basic or above) with AGI Cloud switched on and a routine whose run was missed or skipped by the server
S63.33.note: The note comes from the server's missed-run record, so a tester cannot force a missed run from the app; the mobile rendering is in apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleRunHistory.tsx.
steps: Open Schedules and tap History on a card.
Look at a run row for a note under its status line: Ran late: scheduled for <time>, or Skipped the run scheduled for <time>.
Read the reason in the note (missed by a set amount of time, and whether the schedule skips missed runs).
Compare with Expected: the run history should say that a run was skipped or late and why.
S63.33.where: Open menu > Schedules > card > History > Run History row note
